references.text: The same requirement that the sacrificial animal must be a male without defect is mentioned for cattle as a burnt offering.
Detailed requirements that sacrificial animals must be males without defect from cattle, sheep, or goats.
Small livestock (sheep and goats) are mentioned as acceptable animals for peace offerings, with the requirement that they must be without defect.
A male goat without defect is used as a sin offering.
A lamb without defect is used as a sin offering.
The Passover lamb was to be taken from the sheep or goats, showing that both types of animals were acceptable sacrifices.
Abraham offered a ram as a burnt offering instead of Isaac, an early example of small livestock as a burnt offering.
Christ's sacrifice is described as 'without defect,' fulfilling the Old Testament requirement for unblemished sacrificial animals.
Christ is described as a lamb without defect and without blemish, fulfilling the requirement for a perfect sacrifice.
Comparison of gender requirements for cattle: male (burnt offering) versus male or female (peace offering).
Confirmation of the universal requirement for unblemishedness across all types of sacrifices.
Consistent requirement for unblemished males across different sacrificial categories.
Comparison of requirements for male animals in burnt offerings and guilt offerings.
Specification of the requirement for a male lamb as a burnt offering in Nazirite legislation.
Theological contrast: male for burnt offering versus female for sin offering.
